Surfaced 2026-05-12 by PRINCIPAL during the bw-Ariadne integration arc, after POLYBIUS over-claimed structural sufficiency from a single N=1 observation.

## The discipline

Every CAPTAIN-tier check in the dispatch pipeline (DAEDALUS / ARGUS / ADA / VERA / CATO / ZENO) is structurally redundant by design — multiple seats reading the same artifact from different angles. The redundancy is the safety property, not surplus to be optimized away based on single observations.

When one check catches a defect (and others would have missed it, or didn't dispatch at all), the right conclusion is 'the pipeline worked,' not 'we can drop the other checks.'

## Specific epistemological rule

**Do not generalize from N=1.** A single observation where 'CATO caught X that VERA didn't' or 'ADA shipped clean without DAEDALUS' is one data point — not evidence that the missing seat is structurally unnecessary. Structural claims about the pipeline's safety properties require:

- Multiple observations across distinct defect classes, AND
- Controlled comparison (the same defect class encountered with vs. without the seat in question), AND
- Substrate-level pattern (not just a one-off anecdote in a TIMING_LOG)

Until those conditions are met, the canonical pattern (full gauntlet dispatch) is the default. Per-engagement scope decisions (e.g., 'this is mechanical scaffolding, ADA + CATO only') are operational choices made deliberately, not extrapolations from prior catches.

## Empirical anchor

2026-05-12, ariadne--8fd arc Phase 4 close-out. CATO caught a load-bearing wire-shape mismatch via cold-read in a dispatch scoped as ADA+CATO-only. POLYBIUS initially framed this as 'cold-read is structurally sufficient for this defect class.' PRINCIPAL corrected: catching something once isn't catching it every time. The reframe: 'CATO caught this defect in this instance' (which is honest) vs. 'cold-read alone is sufficient' (which is overreach).

## Substrate touch-points

- **operating-disciplines.md** — add a section on redundancy-discipline + the N=1 generalization rule. Probably alongside or after the gauntlet-shape section.
- **MAJOR_PLINY.md** — orchestrator's dispatch discipline. PLINY should not narrow gauntlet scope based on prior-catch observations alone; scope is an explicit deliberate decision per engagement.
- **MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md** — POLYBIUS authoring timing logs / retrospectives should not enshrine N=1 conclusions as 'lessons learned' that imply structural claims.
- **CAPTAIN envelopes** — every captain knows their dispatch has a purpose even when the other captains caught everything in a given run.

## Gauntlet

ADA + CATO eyeball. Substrate doc-only edit; no code change. ~30-60 LOC across operating-disciplines.md + the role files referenced above.

## Sequencing

P2. Substrate hygiene. Not blocking any in-flight ariadne work; ride with the next substrate-grooming dispatch.

## Out of scope

- Adding more redundant checks (the existing pipeline shape is already redundant; this ticket reinforces it, doesn't expand it)
- Eliminating any existing check (explicitly the opposite — this ticket is about not eliminating them)

## Calibration-discipline addendum: estimate-axis separation

Surfaced 2026-05-12 via the bw → Ariadne integration arcs Phase 4 operator action (HUMAN_relay_substrate_bw_scaling_findings_2026-05-12.md from project-tier).

The arcs calibration data revealed two materially different estimation axes that the substrates redundant-checks discipline should treat separately:

### Axis A: Agent-team throughput

Estimates for gauntlet-shaped agent work (DAEDALUS / ADA / VERA / CATO / etc.) held within ~3x across mechanical-scaffolding and DAEDALUS-designed phases alike. Phase 1+2+3+3.5+4+4.5+5 all came in at 30-90 min of CAPTAIN-agent work against estimates of 1-4 hours. The estimation discipline that produced this calibration is now empirically validated for similar-shape future work.

### Axis B: Upstream-substrate performance characteristics

The Phase 4 OPERATOR ACTION (bulk-seed full Conan corpus through the just-built scripts/seed_bw_corpus.py) was estimated at ~8 min wall-clock on paid Gemini tier. Empirical: ~50-80h projection at the observed superlinear scaling curve, because the underlying bw substrate has a TreeFS.Commit pattern that rewrites the entire tree on every commit. The estimate was off by ~500x because the estimator (POLYBIUS) did not profile the substrate at relevant scale before committing.

### Calibration-discipline rule (new)

**Agent-team throughput and upstream-substrate performance are separate estimation axes. Each requires its own characterization.** A correct estimate for an arc that involves both:

1. Estimate agent-team work (Axis A) — anchor on calibration data from similar-shape past arcs.
2. Estimate upstream-substrate performance (Axis B) — profile the substrate at relevant scale BEFORE committing, especially for bulk operations. Do not extrapolate from small-N behavior unless you have also characterized the scaling curve.
3. Surface both axes separately in the engagement plan, so the reviewer can pressure-test each independently.

The N=1 generalization rule (this tickets original scope) and the estimate-axis-separation rule are complementary disciplines. Both target the same failure mode (drawing structural conclusions from insufficient data), at different layers.

### Empirical anchor

Project-tier relay 2026-05-12; the bw scaling research at agents/research/bw-scaling-vs-mature-systems/scaling-research.md and bw-create-on-source-read/findings.md in ariadne-core-workspace captures the substrate-profiling work that should have happened pre-bulk-seed, not post-discovery.

## Addendum: STRABO source-read claims need cross-verification

Surfaced 2026-05-12 during the bw upstream-bug etiquette exchange.

The HUMAN_relay_substrate_bw_scaling_findings_2026-05-12.md project-tier relay reported a bw upstream bug: "A latent correctness bug at internal/issue/id.go:128 (matches = append(matches, matches) — appends slice to itself instead of appending the matched ID) was also surfaced during the source read."

When substrate-tier POLYBIUS went to draft the GitHub issue, direct verification against jallum/beadwork v0.13.0 tag AND main HEAD showed the code is structurally correct:

```
line 129: matches = append(matches, id)
```

There is no `append(matches, matches)` anywhere in internal/issue/id.go. The bug claim does not hold up under verification.

This is the same N=1 / sufficient-verification failure mode this ticket addresses, applied to STRABO source-read claims:

- STRABO read source and made a claim
- Project-tier POLYBIUS propagated the claim into a substrate-tier relay
- Substrate-tier POLYBIUS almost propagated it to jallum as a GitHub issue

The chain of trust would have ended with PRINCIPAL filing a wrong-bug issue against an actively-maintained upstream project. The only thing that caught it was the substrate-tier POLYBIUS verifying the exact line before drafting (per the "stop guessing, look at the code" discipline PRINCIPAL has been reinforcing all session).

### Discipline addendum

STRABO source-read findings should be CROSS-VERIFIED before propagating to substrate-tier or upstream-projects. The verification can be light (re-grep the cited line; re-check the cited file) but must happen at the propagation boundary.

This complements the existing N=1 rule + estimate-axis rule. The pattern across all three: **agent claims about external state should not become substrate canon (or external action) without independent verification at the propagation boundary.**

### Empirical anchor

2026-05-12 — STRABO's claim about internal/issue/id.go:128 in the project-tier bw scaling research; verified against bw main and v0.13.0 by substrate-tier POLYBIUS at the drafting boundary; claim does not hold up. The TreeFS.Commit scaling-curve claim in the same research artifact is corroborated by independent empirical measurement (2.79s → 21s/ticket observed during bulk-seed); the standalone id.go:128 claim has no such corroboration. Treat verification status as per-claim, not per-research-artifact.

title: Redundant-checks discipline: pipeline redundancy isn't surplus to optimize away
